newsitem.title: GERMANY: Econ conference - EMU timetable must be maintained.
newsitem.headline: Econ conference - EMU timetable must be maintained.

text.p: The timetable for the start of Europe's currency union should be closely maintained and the in no way be open to question, a conference of German regional finance ministers concluded on Friday.

Lothar Klemm, Economics Minister for the state of Hesse and chairman of the conference, said currency union was part of Europe's answer to the globalisation of international markets and was not merely a technical issue.

Any opening up of the timetable could result in a turning away from the policy of reducing debt and tightening fiscal discipline and to speculation on the mark, which would harm the German economy, Klemm said.
Klemm went on to say that Germany as a financial centre, and especially Frankfurt, should be the home market for the euro.
Klemm said the German government had to change all its existing debt to euros in 1999 to ensure Frankfurt's key future role as a financial centre.
